note: Water commitments that no other dataset in this tracker holds: the U.S. federal layer that is not a bill or an executive order (EPA's Water Reuse Action Plan 2.0; the USGS national water availability assessment), international comparators with a real national instrument (the EU's data-centre rating scheme and Water Resilience Strategy; Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap), and local agreements with water terms (community benefits and development agreements, a consent judgment, and one rejected agreement). State commitments are not duplicated here: the Commitments view derives them from the principle tags on enacted state instruments in legislation.json, and company pledges from company_water_claims.json. Researched 2026-09-26 from the Data Center Community Benefits project's water-themed policies (a lead list) plus primary sources; every term was re-read in its source, and records resting on secondary reporting carry confidence 'medium' with a note saying why. Netherlands and Chile were checked and left out: neither has a national data-centre water instrument.

commitments.summary: A collaborative, explicitly non-regulatory framework under existing Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act authority. Data-center cooling is one of the named priority reuse sectors, and Action 3.10 is the closest thing the federal government has to a data-center water commitment: helping states permit reclaimed water for cooling.

terms.text: Compile and share best practices for industrial cooling so states can more readily permit recycled or reclaimed water for data-center cooling (Action 3.10).
Identify, and propose fixes to, the regulatory hurdles that block reuse for data-center cooling.

sources.title: EPA news release — EPA launches Water Reuse Action Plan 2.0

commitments.summary: The federal government's national picture of water supply and demand, which finds about 30 million people live in areas of high water limitation. Data centers do not appear in it as a water-use category or a demand driver — the assessment that would anchor a national strategy does not see them.

terms.text: National supply-and-demand assessment for water years 2010-2020; demand drivers discussed are agriculture, energy production, ecosystems and population growth, not data centers.

sources.title: USGS news release — a comprehensive look at water resources in the United States

commitments.instrument: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 — common Union rating scheme for data centres
commitments.summary: Under the recast Energy Efficiency Directive, every data centre with 500 kW or more of installed IT load must measure and report its total water input and its potable water input, and the Commission computes water usage effectiveness as one of four official sustainability indicators. The EU already has, in binding law, the facility-level water reporting US bills are still proposing — though individual figures stay confidential and only aggregates are published.

terms.text: Mandatory reporting of total water input and potable water input (Annex II) for data centres of 500 kW or more; aggregate WUE published in the European database on data centres.

commitments.summary: A national-scale water strategy that names data centres explicitly, among the strategic sectors that 'consume large volumes of often ultra-pure water'. It commits the Commission to put water usage in the data-centre sustainability rating and to propose minimum water-consumption performance standards for data centres — a move from reporting to an efficiency floor, with no numeric target yet.

terms.text: Include water usage among the parameters of the common Union scheme rating data-centre sustainability.
Propose minimum water-consumption performance standards for data centres (no number set yet).

sources.title: EUR-Lex — European Water Resilience Strategy, COM(2025) 280 final

commitments.actor: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) with the Public Utilities Board
commitments.summary: Sets a national water-use-effectiveness goal: bring data centres from a 2021 median of 2.2 m³/MWh to 2.0 m³/MWh or lower within ten years, mainly by optimizing cooling towers, which are up to 97% of a data centre's water use. Separately and already binding, any site using 60,000 m³ a year or more must meter privately and file a Water Efficiency Plan with PUB.

terms.text: National WUE target of 2.0 m³/MWh or lower within ten years (from a 2.2 m³/MWh median in 2021).
Sites using 60,000 m³ a year or more: private water meters and a Water Efficiency Plan filed with PUB (binding).

commitments.actor: Pima County, AZ and Beale Infrastructure
commitments.summary: After Tucson rejected Project Blue, the county's agreement with the developer commits the campus to closed-loop air cooling, limits water use to domestic needs such as restrooms and kitchens, and requires the Arizona Department of Water Resources to approve its water sources.

terms.text: A closed-loop air-cooling system keeps the facility from overheating.
Water consumption limited to domestic necessities such as bathrooms and kitchens.
Water sources must be approved by the Arizona Department of Water Resources.

sources.title: Arizona Luminaria — Pima County supervisors approve agreement outlining Beale's commitments on Project Blue

commitments.note: The agreement itself is posted as a scanned PDF with no extractable text; terms are as reported by Arizona Luminaria.

commitments.actor: City of Lancaster, PA and CoreWeave / Chirisa Technology Parks
commitments.summary: One of the first data-center community benefits agreements with a numeric water term: the agreement restricts the facility's water use to 20,000 gallons a day.

terms.text: Water use restricted to 20,000 gallons a day.

sources.title: Brookings — Why community benefit agreements are necessary for data centers

commitments.note: The city's posted draft is a compressed PDF with no extractable text; the cap is as reported by Brookings and local coverage.

commitments.actor: Village of Mount Pleasant, WI and Microsoft
commitments.summary: Microsoft's agreement to build on the former Foxconn site pairs the data centers with watershed restoration: $4.2 million to restore 1.5 miles of Lamparek Creek and about 100 acres of surrounding prairie and forest, and $100,000 for water restoration across Racine County.

terms.text: $4.2 million to restore 1.5 miles of Lamparek Creek (about 100 acres of prairie, forest and degraded stream buffer).
$100,000 for water-restoration work across Racine County with the Root-Pike Watershed Initiative Network.

sources.title: WPR — Mount Pleasant approves Microsoft deal for data centers on Foxconn land

commitments.actor: Doña Ana County, NM and Project Jupiter (STACK Infrastructure, BorderPlex Digital)
commitments.instrument: Industrial revenue bond and PILOT agreement (Ordinance 367-2025)
commitments.summary: The campus serving the Oracle and OpenAI Stargate buildout carries the largest water-infrastructure commitment in this record: $50 million for public water and wastewater infrastructure in the Sunland Park and Santa Teresa area, $10 million of it as metrics-driven water-quality grants to Sunland Park, plus $250,000 to evaluate a desalination plant.

terms.text: $50 million for public water and wastewater infrastructure in Doña Ana County.
$10 million of it routed to Sunland Park as a metrics-driven water-quality grant program.
$250,000 to evaluate a desalination plant as a long-term drinking-water source.

sources.title: STACK Infrastructure — $56.9 million in water and community commitments for Doña Ana County
Doña Ana County — economic development projects

commitments.note: The $50 million and $10 million figures come from the developer's release; the county's own page lists the desalination evaluation and generic water and wastewater improvements.

commitments.actor: Saline Township, MI and Related Digital (Oracle-OpenAI Stargate)
commitments.instrument: Consent judgment, Washtenaw County Circuit Court
commitments.summary: The settlement of the rezoning lawsuit bars high-water-use evaporative cooling, limits water use to domestic, humidity, landscaping, fire-protection and maintenance needs (about 20,000 gallons a day anticipated), and preserves 47.5 acres of wetlands under a conservation easement. The facility is not water-free: its air-cooled system circulates a water-refrigerant mix filled from an on-site well.

terms.text: No design containing high-water-use evaporative cooling (Section 3(g)).
Water use limited to restrooms and domestic uses, humidity, landscaping, fire protection and maintenance; about 20,000 gallons a day anticipated.
47.5 acres of wetlands protected by a conservation easement.

sources.title: Saline Township — consent judgment and water FAQ
Planet Detroit — Saline data center settlement challenge

commitments.actor: Frederick County, MD and Quantum Frederick
commitments.instrument: Community benefits agreement ($110 million, never executed)
commitments.summary: County Executive Jessica Fitzwater rejected the proposed agreement amid public outcry. It had offered to shrink planned development by about a fifth and cut potable water use by 80% once a reclaimed-water system came online — commitments that never took effect.

terms.text: Cut potable water use 80% once a reclaimed-water system came online (offered, not adopted).

sources.title: WYPR — Frederick County rejects agreement with data center developer amid public outcry
